findings.title: Nearness becomes the preference criterion
findings.claim: The focus clause presents worldly life as the near or lower pole that is selected, so preference becomes a defective value rule in which proximity outweighs benefit and lastingness.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb carries active ranking, the life noun carries life as benefit and protection, and the final qualifier marks the nearer comparison pole. The supplied preference, life-value, and immediate-versus-later rows make those carriers meet and change a bare report of desire into a diagnosis of its measuring rule.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see that the clause exposes how value is measured: what is close is treated as decisive while benefit and endurance remain the counter-scale.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading that the addressees prefer worldly life remains intact. This is a supplied global valuation resonance, not a universal motive or an exhaustive definition of the words.

epistemic.reason: Trusted support anchors all three focus branches; exact connection rows supply independent comparison triggers.
